title: Adaptive Quantization and Runtime Fallback Standards
author: Ava Patel
body:
Summary:

This document defines the standards for adaptive quantization profiles and the runtime fallback policy used by Redwood's serving runtime. The goal is to allow aggressive cost-optimizing quantization for production traffic while guaranteeing detectable quality regressions are automatically mitigated by deterministic fallback actions.

Scope:

- Applies to all model variants served by Redwood-hosted and Dedicated runtimes.
- Covers quantization profile metadata, runtime quality checks, automated fallback routing, SLOs, testing, and operational monitoring.
- Does NOT replace model onboarding QA; it complements pre-deployment validation with production guards.

Motivation:

Quantization is a major lever for inference cost reduction but can introduce subtle quality regressions that only surface under real traffic. These standards ensure teams can deploy quantized variants safely and recover automatically with documented ownership and observability.

Definitions:

- Quantization profile: A named set of numeric transformations and runtime flags (e.g., int8-aq, int4-ema, q4_0) attached to a model variant.
- Canary prompt-set: A small representative set (default 150 prompts) used at runtime to detect quality drift.
- Quality signal: Metric(s) computed against the canary prompt-set, e.g., token-level perplexity delta, semantic similarity (cosine) for embeddings, or task-specific eval scores.
- Fallback: Automatic routing away from a quantized variant to a less-quantized/FP16 variant or a different model family when thresholds are exceeded.

Standards (high level):

1) Quantization Profile Metadata

- Every quantized model variant MUST include the following metadata fields:
  - profile_name (string): short, kebab-case, e.g. "int8-latency-optimized"
  - compress_rate (string): estimated token-cost reduction, e.g. "~2.6x"
  - expected_p50_latency_ms (string): representative p50 at standard load, e.g. "85ms"
  - predeploy_eval_hash (string): SHA256 of the canonical predeploy eval run
  - fallback_targets (list of strings): ordered model variants to try on fallback, e.g. ["fp16-stable", "int8-conservative"]

- Profiles SHOULD be versioned (profile_name + semantic suffix) when microarchitectural changes occur, e.g. "int8-latency-optimized-v2".

2) Runtime Quality Checks

- The serving runtime MUST execute a lightweight canary evaluation every 60s per model-shard using the canary prompt-set (default: 150 items).
- Quality signals to compute (select at least one per model class):
  - generation: mean normalized perplexity (MNP), normalized against baseline FP16 MNP;
  - semantics/embeddings: mean cosine similarity versus baseline embeddings;
  - classification/regression: micro-F1 or task-specific metric from the suite.
- Check frequency and sample size are configurable per customer model (min interval 30s, max interval 300s).

3) Thresholds and Decision Logic

- Alert threshold (soft): any single 60s canary run that shows:
  - generation: MNP increase >= 7% relative to baseline OR
  - embeddings: mean cosine drop >= 0.06 OR
  - task-F1 drop >= 3% absolute.
- Failure threshold (hard, triggers fallback): aggregated over a 5-minute rolling window: at least 3/5 checks meeting or exceeding the alert thresholds above.
- Safety net: if request error-rate > 0.5% or tail latency (p99) increases > 40% relative to baseline, trigger immediate fallback regardless of canary signals.

4) Fallback Policy (automated)

- When the failure threshold is met, runtime must execute the following deterministic steps in order:
  1. Switch 100% of new traffic for the affected model-shard to the first available fallback_target in metadata.
  2. Maintain sticky in-flight request completion on the original variant for up to 60s to avoid partial-response errors.
  3. Mark the incident in runtime metadata and emit an event to the incident stream with tags: model, profile_name, shard_id, reason, metric_series (last 10 canary runs).
  4. Notify owning team via configured paged channel if the incident persists after 10 minutes.

- Rollback: a successful sequence of 10 consecutive canary checks (per-shard) within 80% of baseline metric values is required before attempting a re-enable of the quantized variant. Re-enable is performed as a canary rollout (5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) with 10-minute stabilization windows.

5) SLOs, Metrics and Alerting

- SLOs to maintain for quantized traffic:
  - Quality SLO: no more than 0.2% of quantized-shard-minute windows per month may exceed the Failure threshold (soft tolerable regressions).
  - Availability SLO: quantized-variants must not cause model-level availability decrease of >0.1% compared to baseline FP16 for the month.

- Required telemetry (emitted per model-shard):
  - canary_mnp_ratio (time-series string), canary_cosine_mean, canary_task_f1, fallback_events.count, fallback_duration_seconds, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, error_rate

- Alerts:
  - Paging: fallback_events.count > 0 for > 10 minutes AND owning_team != "opt-out" triggers page.
  - Ops-only: per-shard p99 latency increase > 40% triggers runbook.

6) Testing and Predeploy Requirements

- Predeploy checklist for any quantized profile:
  1. Run the canonical predeploy eval (1500 prompts) and record predeploy_eval_hash.
  2. Run a micro-benchmark of 1000 production-simulated requests to estimate p50/p95/p99.
  3. Confirm functional parity on a golden prompt-set (team-owned, 300 prompts) with metric deltas under the alert thresholds.
  4. Document fallback_targets and ownership in model manifest.

- Canary prompt-set construction guidance:
  - Minimum 150 items, representative across top 10 intents by traffic, include edge-case prompts known to be fragile.
  - Keep as immutable artifact stored in model revision history.

7) Ownership and Roles

- Owning team: the team that owns the model variant is the primary on-call for fallback notifications.
- Runtime team: implements the canary execution, telemetry, and automatic routing logic.
- SRE: owns the alerting rules and cross-service incident escalation.

8) Operational Runbook (short):

- Trigger: Automatic fallback event emitted for a model-shard.
- Immediate steps (0-10m):
  1. Verify incident details in the runtime incident event.
  2. Check recent canary metric plots for canary_mnp_ratio / canary_cosine_mean.
  3. If fallback restored service and metrics are within baseline, annotate incident and close.
- Remediation (10-60m):
  1. Reproduce failure locally using the canary prompt-set against both quantized and fallback variants.
  2. If reproduction succeeds, collect model logs, kernel traces, and hardware telemetry; open an engineering ticket.
  3. If not reproducible, consider expanding canary set and run a 5k request smoke test.

9) Telemetry retention and privacy

- Canary artifacts and derived metrics are retained for 90 days by default. Raw user inputs used to construct canary prompts must follow the data-retention policy: remove PII and follow the customer data residency constraints.

10) Example configuration snippet (YAML)

  model_id: text-redwood-23b
  variant: int8-latency-optimized-v1
  quantization_profile:
    profile_name: int8-latency-optimized-v1
    compress_rate: "~2.4x"
    expected_p50_latency_ms: "88ms"
    fallback_targets: ["fp16-stable-v3", "int8-conservative-v1"]
    canary_prompt_set_ref: "gs://redwood-canaries/text-redwood-23b/int8-v1/150.json"
    canary_interval_seconds: "60"
    canary_sample_size: "150"
    alert_thresholds:
      generation_mnp_pct: "7"
      embeddings_cosine_drop: "0.06"
      task_f1_drop_pct: "3"

11) CLI / debug commands (examples)

- Trigger a manual canary run:
  rwdctl runtime canary-run --model-id text-redwood-23b --variant int8-latency-optimized-v1 --shard shard-2

- Force fallback for a shard:
  rwdctl runtime fallback --model-id text-redwood-23b --shard shard-2 --target fp16-stable-v3 --reason "manual-testing"

- Inspect last 20 canary results:
  rwdctl runtime canary-list --model-id text-redwood-23b --variant int8-latency-optimized-v1 --limit 20

Appendix A: Example incident event payload (abbreviated JSON for diagnostics)

{
  "event_type": "quant-fallback",
  "model_id": "text-redwood-23b",
  "profile": "int8-latency-optimized-v1",
  "shard": "shard-2",
  "reason": "canary_mnp_rolling_failed",
  "last_canary_metrics": "[...series values omitted here ...]"
}

Notes and rationale:

- Thresholds were chosen to prioritize user-visible quality while allowing meaningful cost reductions; teams operating high-sensitivity verticals (finance/medical/regulatory) should override alert thresholds to be more conservative (e.g., 2–3% generation MNP threshold).
- This standard assumes the runtime can execute lightweight canary evaluations with <1% additional CPU/GPU overhead per-shard; measurement and optimization of that overhead is tracked in a separate infra standard.
